hakka-chinese.name: Hakka Chinese
hakka-chinese.summary: A group of Chinese language varieties spoken natively by the Hakka people across southern China, Taiwan and diaspora communities worldwide, most closely related to Gan.

arthur-robert-kenney-herbert.name: Arthur Robert Kenney-Herbert
arthur-robert-kenney-herbert.summary: A British soldier in the Indian Army (1840–1916) who wrote about cooking, documenting Anglo-Indian cuisine.

hobson-jobson.name: Hobson-Jobson
hobson-jobson.summary: A historical dictionary of Anglo-Indian words and phrases from Indian languages used during British rule, written by Henry Yule and Arthur Coke Burnell and first published in 1886.

orissa-famine-of-1866.name: Orissa Famine of 1866
orissa-famine-of-1866.summary: A famine that struck India's east coast in 1866, killing at least a million people, roughly a third of the population of the hardest-hit region, Odisha.

madras-presidency.name: Madras Presidency
madras-presidency.summary: Administrative region of British India covering most of South India, governed from the city of Madras (Chennai) from the 17th century until Indian independence.

dalcha.name: Dalcha
dalcha.summary: An Indian lentil-based stew from Hyderabad, possibly derived from the Middle Eastern dish harees, typically made with lentils, vegetables or meat and bottle gourd.

sheermal.name: Sheermal
sheermal.summary: A saffron-flavored flatbread from Iran and the Indian subcontinent, introduced to North India by the Mughal emperors and now part of Lucknow, Hyderabad and other regional cuisines.

augustus-prinsep.name: Augustus Prinsep
augustus-prinsep.summary: English artist, writer and civil servant (1803–1830), best known for a posthumously published travel journal.

government-college-of-art-craft.name: Government College of Art & Craft
government-college-of-art-craft.summary: One of the oldest art colleges in India, founded in Kolkata in 1854 to teach industrial art based on scientific methods, later renamed twice before reaching its current name in 1951.

indo-saracenic-architecture.name: Indo-Saracenic architecture
indo-saracenic-architecture.summary: A revivalist building style used mainly by British architects in India in the late 19th century, blending native Indo-Islamic, especially Mughal, elements with Gothic Revival and Neo-Classical forms.

thanjavur-painting.name: Tanjore painting
thanjavur-painting.summary: A classical South Indian painting style from Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu, known for rich colours, gold-foil overlays and inlaid gems, mostly depicting Hindu gods and saints.

bengal-school-of-art.name: Bengal School of Art
bengal-school-of-art.summary: An early 20th-century Indian art movement centered in Calcutta and Shantiniketan, tied to Indian nationalism and led by Abanindranath Tagore.

ernest-binfield-havell.name: Ernest Binfield Havell
ernest-binfield-havell.summary: English arts administrator and art historian (1861–1934) who, as principal of Calcutta's Government School of Art from 1896 to 1905, helped found the Bengal school of art.

abanindranath-tagore.name: Abanindranath Tagore
abanindranath-tagore.summary: Indian painter (1871-1951) who founded the Bengal school of art, led the Indian Society of Oriental Art from 1907, and was also known as a children's writer.

kala-bhavana.name: Kala Bhavana
kala-bhavana.summary: The fine arts faculty of Visva-Bharati University in Shantiniketan, India, founded in 1919 by Nobel laureate Rabindranath Tagore.

william-hodges.name: William Hodges
william-hodges.summary: English painter (1744–1797) who joined James Cook's second Pacific voyage, known for paintings of places he visited including Tahiti, Easter Island and New Zealand.

william-daniell.name: William Daniell
william-daniell.summary: English painter and printmaker (1769–1837) specialising in landscape and marine art, who travelled in India with his uncle Thomas Daniell to produce Oriental Scenery, and later painted Britain's coastline.

thomas-daniell.name: Thomas Daniell
thomas-daniell.summary: An English landscape painter (1749–1840) known for Orientalist themes, who spent seven years in India with his nephew William and published aquatint series of the country.

abdur-rahman-chughtai.name: Abdur Rahman Chughtai
abdur-rahman-chughtai.summary: Pakistani painter regarded as the national artist of Pakistan, who created the influential 'Chughtai Style' blending Mughal, Persian, Bengali and Islamic art traditions.

kshitindranath-mazumdar.name: Kshitindranath Mazumdar
kshitindranath-mazumdar.summary: Indian painter (1891–1975) and key figure of the Bengal School, an art movement that helped shape modern Indian art.

italianate-architecture.name: Italianate architecture
italianate-architecture.summary: A 19th-century architectural style inspired by 16th-century Italian Renaissance buildings, first developed in Britain around 1802 and later hugely popular in the United States.

st-andrew-s-church-chennai.name: St. Andrew's Church, Chennai
st-andrew-s-church-chennai.summary: A church in Egmore, Chennai, built from 1818 to serve the city's Scottish community and modeled on London's St Martin-in-the-Fields.

metcalfe-hall.name: Metcalfe Hall
metcalfe-hall.summary: A mid-19th-century heritage building in Kolkata, built between 1840 and 1844 in British imperial, Greek-temple-inspired style and named after Governor-General Charles T. Metcalfe for his support of a free press.

falaknuma-palace.name: Falaknuma Palace
falaknuma-palace.summary: A palace built in 1893 in Hyderabad, India, by the Paigah family and later owned by the Nizam of Hyderabad; it was the city's tallest building on completion.

art-industrial-school.name: Art Industrial School
art-industrial-school.summary: A private industrial training institute in Nazareth, Tamil Nadu, India.

arthur-margoschis.name: Arthur Margoschis
arthur-margoschis.summary: A Protestant missionary (1852–1908) in India who developed the town of Nazareth in Tamil Nadu, earning the title "Father of Nazareth."

tirunelveli-district.name: Tirunelveli district
tirunelveli-district.summary: A district of Tamil Nadu, India, formed in 1790 by the British East India Company, with the city of Tirunelveli as its headquarters.

mysore-painting.name: Mysore school of painting
mysore-painting.summary: A classical South Indian painting style centred on Mysore, Karnataka, known for elegance and muted colours, which evolved from the Vijayanagara school after that empire fell in 1565.

krishnaraja-wodeyar-iii.name: Krishnaraja Wodeyar III
krishnaraja-wodeyar-iii.summary: 22nd Maharaja of Mysore, who ruled for nearly seventy years from 1799 to 1868 and was known for his patronage of the arts and music.

shivaji-of-thanjavur.name: Shivaji of Thanjavur
shivaji-of-thanjavur.summary: A Raja of the Bhonsle dynasty who ruled the fortress of Thanjavur in India from 1832 to 1855, the last Raja of Thanjavur known to hold real authority.

serfoji-ii.name: Serfoji II
serfoji-ii.summary: Last sovereign ruler of the Maratha principality of Thanjavur, reigning 1787–1793 and 1798–1832, remembered for patronizing art and culture and for work in ophthalmology.

nataraja.name: Nataraja
nataraja.summary: A depiction of the Hindu god Shiva as cosmic dancer, one of the most recognized symbols of Hindu art, especially in bronze sculptures from the Chola period.

meerut.name: Meerut
meerut.summary: A city in Uttar Pradesh, India, and site of the 1857 mutiny by East India Company sepoys that sparked the wider Indian Rebellion of 1857.

second-anglo-sikh-war.name: Second Anglo-Sikh War
second-anglo-sikh-war.summary: A conflict from 1848 to 1849 between the Sikh Empire and the East India Company that ended with the fall of the Sikh Empire and Britain's annexation of the Punjab.

oudh-state.name: Oudh State
oudh-state.summary: A former Mughal province that became an independent kingdom in North India, then a British protectorate annexed by the East India Company in 1856, with its capital at Faizabad.

bahadur-shah-zafar.name: Bahadur Shah Zafar
bahadur-shah-zafar.summary: The twentieth and last Mughal emperor (1775–1862) and an Urdu poet, declared Emperor of India during the 1857 rebellion before being exiled, ending the nearly 500-year Timurid dynasty founded by Timur.

zeenat-mahal.name: Zeenat Mahal
zeenat-mahal.summary: A wife of the last Mughal emperor Bahadur Shah Zafar who served as de facto regent of the Mughal Empire on his behalf.

first-anglo-sikh-war.name: First Anglo-Sikh War
first-anglo-sikh-war.summary: War fought 1845–1846 between the Sikh Empire and the British Empire around Punjab, ending in the Sikhs' defeat and the cession of Jammu and Kashmir.

doaba.name: Doaba
doaba.summary: A region of Punjab, India, between the Beas and Sutlej rivers, also known as Bist Doab or the Jalandhar Doab.

gulab-singh.name: Gulab Singh
gulab-singh.summary: First maharaja of Jammu and Kashmir (1792–1857), originally a Sikh Empire commander who sided with the British and signed the 1846 Treaty of Amritsar establishing his state.

anglo-nepalese-war.name: Anglo-Nepalese War
anglo-nepalese-war.summary: A war fought from 1814 to 1816 between the Kingdom of Nepal and the British East India Company over a disputed Himalayan border, sparked by an attack on British outposts in 1814.

gurkha.name: Gurkha
gurkha.summary: Soldiers native to Nepal and parts of North India, recruited into several national armies and known for a reputation of fearless fighting.

gwalior.name: Gwalior
gwalior.summary: A major city in central India, ruled over the centuries by dynasties from the Gurjara Pratihara to the Mughals and Marathas, later a princely state under British rule.

bakht-khan.name: Bakht Khan
bakht-khan.summary: Commander-in-chief of the Indian rebel forces in Delhi during the 1857 uprising against the East India Company, a former Company officer with forty years' artillery experience.

nana-saheb-peshwa-ii.name: Nana Sahib
nana-saheb-peshwa-ii.summary: Indian aristocrat, born 1824, who led the Siege of Cawnpore during the 1857 rebellion against the East India Company before disappearing after the British retook the city.

9th-queen-s-royal-lancers.name: 9th Lancers
9th-queen-s-royal-lancers.summary: A British Army cavalry regiment first raised in 1715 that served for three centuries, including both World Wars, before merging with another regiment in 1960.

shah-alam-ii.name: Shah Alam II
shah-alam-ii.summary: Seventeenth Mughal emperor (1728–1806) whose reign saw invasions by Ahmad Shah Abdali, defeat at the Battle of Buxar in 1764, and the eventual British capture of Delhi.

yashwantrao-holkar.name: Yashwantrao Holkar
yashwantrao-holkar.summary: Raja of Indore State (1776-1811) and Maratha military leader who fought the British in the Second Anglo-Maratha War, winning recognition as an independent sovereign ruler.

david-ochterlony.name: David Ochterlony
david-ochterlony.summary: A Bengal Army officer (1758–1825), born in Boston, who served as British resident to the Mughal court in Delhi and saw action in numerous conflicts in India.

gerard-lake-1st-viscount-lake.name: Gerard Lake
gerard-lake-1st-viscount-lake.summary: British general (1744-1808) who commanded forces during the Irish Rebellion of 1798 and the Second Anglo-Maratha War, later serving as Commander-in-Chief in British India.

indian-order-of-merit.name: Indian Order of Merit
indian-order-of-merit.summary: A military and civilian decoration of British India established in 1837, long the highest award a native soldier in the British Indian Army could receive.

first-anglo-burmese-war.name: First Anglo-Burmese War
first-anglo-burmese-war.summary: War fought 1824–1826 between the British and Burmese empires, ending in a costly but decisive British victory that gave Britain control of Assam and other regions.

sangam-literature.name: Sangam literature
sangam-literature.summary: The earliest known literature of South India, composed in classical Tamil, with most scholars dating its historical era to roughly 300 BCE to 300 CE.

kumbakonam.name: Kumbakonam
kumbakonam.summary: City in Tamil Nadu, India, known as a "temple city" for its many Hindu shrines, historically ruled by the Cholas, Pandyas and others, and called the "Cambridge of South India" under British rule.

rabindranath-tagore.name: Rabindranath Tagore
rabindranath-tagore.summary: Bengali poet, writer and figure of the Bengal Renaissance who in 1913 became the first Indian and non-European Nobel laureate, winning the Nobel Prize in Literature.

gitanjali.name: Gitanjali
gitanjali.summary: A poetry collection by Rabindranath Tagore whose English translation won him the 1913 Nobel Prize in Literature, the first awarded to an Asian writer.

arumuka-navalar.name: Arumuka Navalar
arumuka-navalar.summary: Sri Lankan Tamil scholar and religious reformer (1822–1879) who revived Hindu Shaivism and pioneered printing Tamil classics amid Christian missionary rivalry.

kural.name: Kural
kural.summary: Classic Tamil text of 1,330 couplets on virtue, wealth and love, traditionally attributed to Valluvar and dated between 300 BCE and 500 CE, praised as the "Tamil Veda".

jaffna.name: Jaffna
jaffna.summary: Capital of Sri Lanka's Northern Province and a long-contested city, once capital of the medieval Tamil Jaffna Kingdom and later held by Portuguese, Dutch and British colonizers.

shaivism.name: Shaivism
shaivism.summary: A branch of Hindu tradition worshipping Shiva as the supreme being, rooted in Vedic worship of Rudra, which became dominant in several Hindu kingdoms and later spread into Southeast Asia.

charyapada.name: Charyapada
charyapada.summary: A collection of mystical Vajrayāna Buddhist poems compiled around 1000–1200 CE, an early record of Eastern Indo-Aryan languages, rediscovered in the early 20th century.

hara-prasad-shastri.name: Hara Prasad Shastri
hara-prasad-shastri.summary: Indian Sanskrit scholar, archivist and historian of Bengali literature (1853–1931), also known as Hara Prasad Bhattacharya.

tirumuruk-uppa-ai.name: Tirumurukāṟṟuppaṭai
tirumuruk-uppa-ai.summary: An ancient Tamil devotional poem entirely dedicated to the god Murugan, describing his shrines and temples; composed by Nakkiranar and dated to roughly the 2nd to 4th century CE.

ten-idylls.name: Ten Idylls
ten-idylls.summary: An anthology of ten long poems from early Tamil Sangam literature, composed roughly between the 2nd and 5th centuries CE, including guides for bards and to religious devotion.

c-w-thamotharampillai.name: C. W. Thamotharampillai
c-w-thamotharampillai.summary: Tamil scholar (1832–1901) considered the first to pioneer the rediscovery of the earliest classical Tamil literature through editing and publishing old texts.

cilappatikaram.name: Cilappatikaram
cilappatikaram.summary: An ancient Tamil epic poem of 5,730 lines, probably composed in the 5th century CE, telling the tragic love story of Kannaki and her husband Kōvalan.

manimekalai.name: Manimekalai
manimekalai.summary: A Tamil Buddhist epic composed between the 2nd and 6th centuries, telling of a dancer-nun who resists a prince's advances and seeks to free herself from worldly ties.

tolk-ppiyam.name: Tolkāppiyam
tolk-ppiyam.summary: The oldest surviving Tamil grammar text and the oldest extant work of Tamil literature, covering phonology, morphology, and poetics; dated as early as the 2nd century BCE by some scholars.

pati-uppattu.name: Patiṟṟuppattu
pati-uppattu.summary: A classical Tamil Chera poetic work, one of the Eight Anthologies of Sangam literature, containing praise poems about generations of Chera kings.

purananuru.name: Purananuru
purananuru.summary: A classical Tamil poetic anthology of 400 heroic poems about kings, wars and public life, composed by 157 poets and traditionally the last of the Eight Anthologies of Sangam literature.

ainkurunuru.name: Ainkurunuru
ainkurunuru.summary: A classical Tamil anthology of 500 short love poems grouped by landscape, likely composed between about 100 BCE and the 4th century CE as part of the Sangam literature.

great-trigonometrical-survey.name: Great Trigonometrical Survey
great-trigonometrical-survey.summary: A project begun in 1802 to survey the Indian subcontinent with scientific precision, which measured the height of the Himalayan peaks Everest, K2 and Kangchenjunga.

survey-of-india.name: Survey of India
survey-of-india.summary: India's central mapping and surveying agency, set up in 1767 to help the British East India Company consolidate its territories; one of the oldest engineering departments of the Government of India.

daguerreotype.name: Daguerreotype
daguerreotype.summary: The first publicly available photographic process, invented by Louis Daguerre and introduced in 1839, made by treating a silver-plated copper plate to record an image, in use until the 1850s.

william-lambton.name: William Lambton
william-lambton.summary: English soldier, surveyor and geographer (c. 1753–1823) who began the Great Trigonometrical Survey of India in 1800, triangulating the subcontinent; his assistant George Everest later succeeded him.

george-everest.name: George Everest
george-everest.summary: British surveyor and geographer (1790–1866) who served as Surveyor General of India, leading a decades-long meridian survey; Mount Everest was later named in his honour.

john-mccosh.name: John McCosh
john-mccosh.summary: Scottish army surgeon who photographed the Second Anglo-Sikh War (1848–1849) and Second Anglo-Burmese War, regarded by some historians as the first named war photographer.

calotype.name: Calotype
calotype.summary: An early photographic process introduced in 1841 using paper coated with silver iodide; its name comes from Greek words meaning 'beautiful impression.'

duleep-singh.name: Duleep Singh
duleep-singh.summary: Last Maharaja of the Sikh Empire (1838–1893), placed on the throne at age five, later deposed and exiled to Britain, where he was befriended by Queen Victoria.

sikh-empire.name: Sikh Empire
sikh-empire.summary: A regional power in the Punjab from 1799 to 1849, founded by Maharaja Ranjit Singh and eventually defeated and annexed by the British East India Company.

bikram-singh-bedi.name: Bikram Singh Bedi
bikram-singh-bedi.summary: A direct lineal descendant of Guru Nanak who died in 1862 and rebelled against British colonial rule during the Second Anglo-Sikh War and the early years after the Sikh Empire's 1849 annexation.

jind-kaur.name: Jind Kaur
jind-kaur.summary: Regent, and briefly ruler, of the Sikh Empire from 1843 to 1847 and mother of its last Maharaja, Duleep Singh; the British later imprisoned and exiled her.

mulraj-chopra.name: Mulraj Chopra
mulraj-chopra.summary: Sikh Empire administrator who governed Multan as Diwan from 1844 to 1849 and led a Sikh rebellion against the British that triggered the Second Anglo-Sikh War.

amritsar.name: Amritsar
amritsar.summary: The second-largest city in the Indian state of Punjab, home to the Golden Temple, the holiest site in Sikhism.

felice-beato.name: Felice Beato
felice-beato.summary: An Italian-British photographer (c. 1832–1909) and pioneer of war and travel photography, among the first to photograph East Asia, known for images of events including the Indian Rebellion of 1857 and the Second Opium War.

nihang.name: Nihang
nihang.summary: A martial order of Sikhs, also called Akali, known for fierce fighting skill and forming guerrilla units of the Sikh Empire's army.

4th-horse-hodson-s-horse.name: Hodson's Horse
4th-horse-hodson-s-horse.summary: An irregular cavalry regiment of the Indian Army that began during the Indian Rebellion of 1857, later becoming part of the Armoured Corps.

samuel-bourne.name: Samuel Bourne
samuel-bourne.summary: A British photographer known for his work in India from 1863 to 1870, who co-founded the photography firm Bourne & Shepherd.

bourne-shepherd.name: Bourne & Shepherd
bourne-shepherd.summary: An Indian photographic studio founded in 1863, one of the world's oldest, that became the most successful commercial photography firm in 19th- and early 20th-century India before closing in 2016.

herbert-ponting.name: Herbert Ponting
herbert-ponting.summary: English photographer (1870–1935) best known as expedition photographer on Robert Falcon Scott's 1910–1913 Terra Nova Antarctic expedition.

queen-victoria.name: Queen Victoria
queen-victoria.summary: Queen of the United Kingdom from 1837 to 1901, whose 63-year reign, longer than any predecessor's, saw great expansion of the British Empire; she was proclaimed Empress of India in 1876.

east-india-company.name: East India Company
east-india-company.summary: An English, later British, trading company founded in 1600 that grew to rule large parts of the Indian subcontinent, with its own armies, before dissolving in 1874.

british-raj.name: British Raj
british-raj.summary: Period of direct rule by the British Crown over the Indian subcontinent, from 1858 until 1947, when it was partitioned into India and Pakistan.

indian-rebellion-of-1857.name: Indian Rebellion of 1857
indian-rebellion-of-1857.summary: A major uprising against East India Company rule that began as a sepoy mutiny in Meerut in May 1857 and was suppressed by mid-1858, also called the Sepoy Mutiny or First War of Independence.

presidencies-and-provinces-of-british-in.name: British India
presidencies-and-provinces-of-british-in.summary: The areas of the Indian subcontinent under direct British governance between 1757 and 1947, distinct from the princely states ruled by indigenous rulers under British oversight.
presidencies-and-provinces-of-british-in.source_title: Presidencies and provinces of British India

princely-state.name: Princely state
princely-state.summary: A nominally sovereign entity of British India governed by an indigenous ruler under British paramountcy, allowed self-governance but barred from foreign relations or wars with other such states.

suzerainty.name: British paramountcy
suzerainty.summary: A relationship in which a dominant power controls a subordinate state's foreign policy and economy while allowing internal self-rule, as with Britain and India's princely states.

north-western-provinces.name: North-Western Provinces
north-western-provinces.summary: Administrative region of British India established in 1836, later merged with the annexed kingdom of Oudh in 1858 and reorganised as the United Provinces of Agra and Oudh in 1902.

sindh.name: Sindh
sindh.summary: A province of Pakistan along the Indus River, home to early South Asian settlement and later conquered by Arab forces in 712 CE.

north-west-frontier-province.name: North-West Frontier Province
north-west-frontier-province.summary: Province of British India from 1901 and later of Pakistan, formed from northwestern Punjab districts with its capital at Peshawar; renamed Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in 2010.

george-curzon-1st-marquess-curzon-of-ked.name: Lord Curzon
george-curzon-1st-marquess-curzon-of-ked.summary: British statesman and Conservative politician (1859–1925) who served as Viceroy of India from 1899 to 1905 and Foreign Secretary from 1919 to 1924.
george-curzon-1st-marquess-curzon-of-ked.source_title: George Curzon, 1st Marquess Curzon of Kedleston

bengal-presidency.name: Bengal Presidency
bengal-presidency.summary: The largest of British India's three presidencies, at its height covering much of South and Southeast Asia, with Calcutta as its capital until 1911.

eastern-bengal-and-assam.name: Eastern Bengal and Assam
eastern-bengal-and-assam.summary: A province of British India from 1905 to 1912, created by splitting Bengal, headquartered at Dacca and covering parts of today's Bangladesh and Northeast India.

partition-of-bengal-1905.name: Partition of Bengal (1905)
partition-of-bengal-1905.summary: The 1905 division of the Bengal Presidency by Viceroy Lord Curzon into Muslim-majority and Hindu-majority provinces, reversed by Britain in 1911 after protests.

pindari.name: Pindaris
pindari.summary: Irregular, unpaid horsemen who rode with Mughal and later Maratha armies from the 17th century, living off plunder until eliminated in the 1817–19 Pindari War.

third-anglo-maratha-war.name: Third Anglo-Maratha War
third-anglo-maratha-war.summary: The final, decisive 1817–1819 conflict between the British East India Company and the Maratha Empire, ending in British control of most of India.

rajput.name: Rajput
rajput.summary: A large cluster of warrior-associated castes and clans from northern India whose kingdoms shaped much of central and northern India from the 7th century onward.

gilbert-elliot-murray-kynynmound-4th-ear.name: Lord Minto
gilbert-elliot-murray-kynynmound-4th-ear.summary: British peer and politician (1845 to 1914) who served as Governor General of Canada from 1898 to 1904 and Viceroy of India from 1905 to 1910.

all-india-muslim-league.name: All-India Muslim League
all-india-muslim-league.summary: Political party in British India, active from 1906 to 1947, that advocated for Muslim interests and led the movement to create Pakistan.

dhaka.name: Dhaka (Dacca)
dhaka.summary: Former name of Dhaka, now the capital of Bangladesh; it grew from the 17th century as a Mughal provincial capital and trading hub, once one of the world's most prosperous cities.

james-broun-ramsay-1st-marquess-of-dalho.name: Marquess of Dalhousie
james-broun-ramsay-1st-marquess-of-dalho.summary: A Scottish statesman who served as Governor-General of India (1848-1856), introducing passenger trains, the electric telegraph and uniform postage.

dogra-dynasty.name: Dogra dynasty
dogra-dynasty.summary: A Rajput dynasty founded by Gulab Singh that created the princely state of Jammu and Kashmir through 19th-century treaties with the East India Company, ruling until 1947.

jammu.name: Jammu
jammu.summary: City on the Tawi River in Jammu and Kashmir, known as the 'City of Temples' and serving as the territory's winter capital.

rajputana-agency.name: Rajputana Agency
rajputana-agency.summary: A British Indian political office overseeing more than 20 princely states in Rajputana, including Udaipur, Jaipur, Bikaner and Jodhpur.

kingdom-of-mewar.name: Kingdom of Mewar
kingdom-of-mewar.summary: An independent Hindu kingdom in Rajasthan founded by the Guhila dynasty, rising to prominence under Bappa Rawal in the 7th century and later ruled by the Sisodia dynasty.

bikaner-state.name: Bikaner State
bikaner-state.summary: A princely state in north-western Rajputana from 1818 to 1947, founded by Rao Bika, which became a loyal constituent of the Mughal Empire and later joined independent India.

kingdom-of-marwar.name: Kingdom of Marwar
kingdom-of-marwar.summary: Also called Jodhpur State, a kingdom in the Marwar region of India from 1243 to 1818, ruled by the Rathore clan, that resisted Mughal rule before becoming a British princely state.

charter-act-1813.name: Charter Act 1813
charter-act-1813.summary: An 1813 act of the UK Parliament that renewed the East India Company's charter but ended its trade monopoly, opening India as a market for British goods.

second-anglo-afghan-war.name: Second Anglo-Afghan War
second-anglo-afghan-war.summary: A war fought between the British Raj and the Emirate of Afghanistan from 1878 to 1880, part of the Great Game between the British and Russian empires.

neo-vedanta.name: Neo-Vedanta
neo-vedanta.summary: 19th-century reinterpretations of Hinduism blending Western ideas with traditional Advaita Vedanta, developed in response to colonialism and championed by figures like Vivekananda.

hindu-reform-movements.name: Hindu modernism
hindu-reform-movements.summary: A set of movements, also called Hindu reform movements or neo-Hinduism, that began during the Bengali Renaissance and sought to renew Hinduism in religious and social terms.

vedanta.name: Vedanta
vedanta.summary: One of the six orthodox schools of Hindu philosophy, meaning 'conclusion of the Vedas,' interpreting the Upanishads, Brahma Sutras and Bhagavad Gita through many later traditions.

swami-vivekananda.name: Swami Vivekananda
swami-vivekananda.summary: Indian Hindu monk (1863–1902) and chief disciple of Ramakrishna who introduced Vedanta and Yoga to the West, notably at the 1893 Parliament of the World's Religions in Chicago.

advaita-vedanta.name: Advaita Vedanta
advaita-vedanta.summary: Hindu philosophical tradition holding that the individual self is ultimately identical with the universal Brahman, and that liberation comes from realizing this oneness.

brahmo-samaj.name: Brahmo Samaj
brahmo-samaj.summary: A monotheistic reformist religious movement founded in Calcutta in 1828 by Raja Ram Mohan Roy and Dwarkanath Tagore, influential in the Bengal Renaissance.

raja-ram-mohan-roy.name: Ram Mohan Roy
raja-ram-mohan-roy.summary: Indian social reformer and writer (1772–1833), a founder of the Brahmo Sabha reform movement, dubbed the 'Father of the Indian Renaissance' for campaigning against sati and child marriage.

theosophical-society.name: Theosophical Society
theosophical-society.summary: The organizational body of Theosophy, founded in New York in 1875 by Helena Blavatsky and Henry Steel Olcott, later splitting into branches in India and California.

bankim-chandra-chatterjee.name: Bankim Chandra Chatterjee
bankim-chandra-chatterjee.summary: Bengali novelist, poet, essayist and journalist (1838–1894) who supported British rule, wrote the 1882 novel Anandamath, and composed the song Vande Mataram.

dharma.name: Dharma
dharma.summary: A central concept in Indian religions meaning one's moral duties and righteous conduct, and the order sustaining life and the universe; it appears in the earliest Vedic texts.

david-lorenzen.name: David Lorenzen
david-lorenzen.summary: A British-American historian and scholar of religious studies specializing in South Asian history, known for his work on the history of Hinduism and Christian missions in India.

sarvepalli-radhakrishnan.name: Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan
sarvepalli-radhakrishnan.summary: Indian philosopher and statesman who served as Vice President (1952–1962) and President of India (1962–1967), reinterpreted Advaita Vedanta for modern readers, and was seen as a bridge between Indian and Western thought.

presidency-college-chennai.name: Presidency College, Chennai
presidency-college-chennai.summary: A government arts, commerce and science college in Chennai, India, established in 1840 as one of the country's oldest such colleges.

buddhist-modernism.name: Buddhist modernism
buddhist-modernism.summary: New reinterpretations of Buddhism shaped by engagement with Western monotheism, scientific naturalism and Romanticism, de-emphasizing traditional doctrine and ritual.

anagarika-dharmapala.name: Anagarika Dharmapala
anagarika-dharmapala.summary: Sri Lankan Buddhist revivalist and writer (1864–1933) who was a major reformer of Sinhala Buddhism and inspired a mass movement of South Indian Dalits to embrace Buddhism decades before B. R. Ambedkar.

henry-steel-olcott.name: Henry Steel Olcott
henry-steel-olcott.summary: American military officer and co-founder of the Theosophical Society who became the first well-known American convert to Buddhism and helped revive Buddhism in Sri Lanka.

hindu-mela.name: Hindu Mela
hindu-mela.summary: An annual political and cultural festival held in India from 1867 to about 1880, promoting sports, indigenous arts and nationalistic poetry to build unity among Indians.

akhara.name: Akhara
akhara.summary: An Indian place of training and lodging for martial artists or religious renunciates in the Guru-shishya tradition, combining physical and monastic practice, as among trident-wielding sadhus of the Dashanami Sampradaya.
